title: Semantic Crosswalk and Type-Separation Canon Locks: Load-Bearing Terms, Phase Boundaries, and Non-Substitution Rules for the Applicability Boundary Doctrine
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
methodology: It consolidates the semantic architecture of the Applicability Boundary Doctrine corpus. It fixes the load‑bearing lexicon, separates authority and phase types, records the non‑substitution canon, and defines conflict rules for future publications in the line.
advantages: It makes the substitution visible and names it as a defect.
critique: The record is purely definitional and does not provide empirical validation or case studies, making it difficult to assess the practical impact of the proposed semantic architecture.
results: It records a twenty‑one‑line non‑substitution canon, seven cross‑publication conflict rules, a lifecycle‑assurance boundary, six interpretation states, integration controls, and a falsification surface of eight conditions under which the record is to be narrowed, revised, or withdrawn.
limitations: It introduces no new doctrine, specifies no runtime enforcement, and introduces no controller.

title: The worldview influence on the internal beliefs of law enforcement agents in the context of exercising their discretionary powers
venue: Ûridičnij časopis Nacìonalʹnoï akademìï vnutrìšnìh sprav
methodology: Used analysis, synthesis, and generalisation methods, including deductive logical analysis, inductive generalisation, and analogy, to process the bibliography and substantiate the results.
advantages: Results can inform changes to legislation on assessing candidates for discretionary positions by focusing on their value beliefs and worldview.
critique: The study relies solely on literature review and logical analysis without empirical data or quantitative evaluation, limiting the ability to validate the claimed influence of worldview on decision-making.
results: Found that scholars have studied worldview and internal conviction separately, and that internal conviction is primarily based on a person's values and worldview formed in childhood, potentially leading to procedural decisions contrary to case facts.

title: A Silent Multi-Agent Recommendation Engine with Graph-Augmented Memory for Immersive B2B E-Commerce
venue: DROPS (Schloss Dagstuhl – Leibniz Center for Informatics)
methodology: Orchestrated via a LangGraph Directed Acyclic Graph, the system utilises Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to dynamically synthesise behavioural signals, dense vector retrieval (Qdrant), and knowledge graph traversal (Apache AGE). A locally hosted Llama 3.1 8B model autonomously extracts implicit user preferences to update a persistent graph database and generates deterministic, human‑readable explanations for each recommendation. A two‑shot verifier engineering pattern is introduced to resolve the structural incompatibility between dynamic candidate sets and static graph execution.
advantages: Operates without explicit textual input; high retrieval accuracy; strict constraint adherence (stock and availability verification); sub‑4‑second end‑to‑end latency when the generative semantic justification step is bypassed; no external API dependencies.
critique: The evaluation relies solely on a controlled synthetic B2B product dataset, which may not reflect the complexities and noise of real‑world industrial e‑commerce environments, limiting confidence in the system's practical effectiveness.
metrics: retrieval accuracy; constraint adherence; end-to-end latency
results: High retrieval accuracy, strict constraint adherence (stock and availability verification), and sub‑4‑second end‑to‑end latency when the generative semantic justification step is bypassed.

title: TDD-Agent: Test-Driven Reasoning for Code Generation
methodology: TDD-Agent first prompts the model to generate executable tests to clarify expected behaviors, then performs iterative dual‑track refinement of both the generated code and the tests using execution feedback.
advantages: Operationalizes test‑driven development for code generation, consistently improves upon reasoning‑based prompting baselines, outperforms retrieval‑based and agent‑based baselines, and iterative refinement yields higher pass rates, coverage, and mutation scores.
critique: While the dual‑track iterative refinement can improve correctness, it may substantially increase computational cost and latency, and the approach still depends on the quality of initially generated tests, which could propagate errors if the tests are misleading.
results: TDD‑Agent consistently improves upon reasoning‑based prompting baselines on LiveCodeBench and outperforms retrieval‑based and agent‑based baselines on RepoEval, with higher pass rates, coverage, and mutation scores.

title: The Completeness Gap: Coverage Failures at Every Layer of an Agentic LLM Research Pipeline
methodology: Empirical case study across three successive system architectures: (1) a self‑directed LLM search with a stopping criterion, (2) a deterministic non‑LLM pre‑fetch of an authoritative source combined with a mandatory reconciliation checklist, and (3) a deterministic third‑generation architecture that removes LLM‑driven table extraction and uses a "most recently filed wins" version‑selection heuristic.
advantages: Deterministic pre‑fetch with a reconciliation checklist more than triples measured coverage (9 to 28 events).
disadvantages: A completeness gap recurs at every layer of the pipeline, and the self‑directed search‑stopping criterion does not scale with true task size.
critique: The study is based on a single empirical case and lacks statistical power, so the observed gaps and improvements may not generalize to other domains or tasks.
datasets: large structured disclosure table; authoritative source
metrics: coverage percentage; event count; portfolio value captured
results: The self‑directed LLM search captured only 9 of 16 known events (56%) on a high‑activity subject and 0% of line items in a structured disclosure table. Replacing it with deterministic pre‑fetch increased coverage from 9 to 28 events. A naive entity‑name query missed 4 of 5 known records, and a 1,000‑record pagination cap would have discarded 69% of a subject's history. The deterministic third‑generation version‑selection heuristic captured only 1 of 10 real holdings (3.8% of true portfolio value).
limitations: The work is presented as an empirical case study rather than a statistically powered benchmark, and the authors note that follow‑up measurement is needed to confirm the central finding.

title: Entity Linking with Wikidata: A Systematic Literature Review
methodology: Systematic literature review that extends previous studies from two to eight dimensions of entity linking (definitions, tasks, types, domains, approaches, datasets, applications, challenges).
advantages: Provides a comprehensive systematic review of entity linking using Wikidata and expands the analysis to eight dimensions, offering a broader overview of the field.
critique: As a review paper, it does not present new empirical experiments or quantitative evaluations, so its conclusions rely on the selected literature and may be subject to selection bias.
results: Datasets primarily address question-answering and news domains but underutilize Wikidata’s capabilities for hyper-relations, multilingualism, and time dependence; research gaps include the need for more robust datasets, hybrid rule‑based and learning‑based methods, and better handling of ambiguity, sparse entity types, data noise, and knowledge‑graph evolution.

title: Duplicated or cloned preprints: the lack of across-the-board ethical regulation of preprint servers may risk leading to citation-abusive and curriculum vitae-enhancing practices
critique: The paper raises important ethical concerns but offers no empirical data, systematic analysis, or concrete case studies to quantify how widespread preprint cloning is or to measure its actual impact on citations and academic CVs, limiting the strength of its arguments.

title: From Verbatim to Gist: Distilling Pyramidal Multimodal Memory via Semantic Information Bottleneck for Long-Horizon Video Agents
methodology: MM-Mem is a pyramidal multimodal memory architecture grounded in Fuzzy-Trace Theory that hierarchically structures memory into a Sensory Buffer, Episodic Stream, and Symbolic Schema, progressively distilling fine‑grained perceptual traces (verbatim) into high‑level semantic schemas (gist). A Semantic Information Bottleneck objective and the SIB‑GRPO optimizer govern memory construction, while an entropy‑driven top‑down retrieval strategy is used at inference time.
advantages: The hierarchical, cognition‑inspired memory organization reduces redundancy and detail loss, enabling efficient long‑horizon video understanding and robust generalization across tasks.
critique: The abstract provides no quantitative analysis of computational overhead or memory footprint, making it unclear how the proposed architecture scales to very long videos or resource‑constrained settings. Moreover, the claim of state‑of‑the‑art performance is based on only four unnamed benchmarks, limiting assessment of generality.
results: MM-Mem achieves state-of-the-art performance on both offline and streaming tasks, demonstrating robust generalization.
extraction_note: abstract only, no detailed methods, metrics, or explicit limitations provided
